item.text:
**Verdict:** Weaker. The 2024 record shows tighter Party control, fewer public accountability venues, more legal/administrative repression in Hong Kong and on the mainland, and no credible evidence of an improved succession or democratic-resilience trajectory. The only pro-side items are official participation rhetoric and procedural choreography, not real strengthening.

| Valence | Title | Publisher | Date | Recoverable URL | Claim-level summary | IDs |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|---|---|
| Weak positive / formalism | **NPC session still followed formal procedure** | Xinhua | 2024-03-04 | https://english.news.cn/20240304/c7ae314c2c8b42d297f49f840e2ba916/c.html | Deputies elected a presidium and set the agenda, so formal parliamentary procedure continued. This shows ritual continuity, not stronger democratic resilience. | 4B.10, 4B.8 |
| Weak positive / self-description | **China’s “whole-process people’s democracy” is real democracy** | PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs | 2024-06-03 | https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/eng/wjb/zygy/hd/202406/t20240603_11374914.html | The ministry claims people elect deputies at multiple levels and that the system is democratic. This is regime self-description, not evidence that political freedom or contestability actually improved. | 4B.10, 4B.1 |
| Strong negative | **China passes law granting Communist Party more control over cabinet** | Reuters | 2024-03-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/china-passes-law-granting-communist-party-more-control-over-cabinet-3331891 | Reuters said the amended State Council Organic Law increased Party control over the cabinet and stressed Party central leadership. That is a direct move toward tighter political control, not resilience. | 4B.10, 4B.5, 4B.8 |
| Strong negative | **China cancels premier's annual press conference for first time since 1993** | Reuters | 2024-03-04 | https://www.investing.com/news/economy/china-cancels-premiers-press-conference-for-first-time-since-1993-3322647 | Removing one of the few recurring accountability venues reduces transparency and public scrutiny. That weakens institutional resilience, not strengthens it. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.8 |
| Strong negative | **China’s Xi grooms next-generation party leaders, but no anointed heir yet** | The Straits Times | 2024-03-03 | https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/china-s-xi-grooms-next-generation-party-leaders-but-no-anointed-heir-yet | Reports Xi had not named a successor and was instead grooming loyal cadres. That is evidence against orderly succession and against durable democratic resilience. | 4B.10, 4B.8 |
| Strong negative | **Choreographed political meet carries message of control** | Reuters | 2024-03-11 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/chinas-choreographed-political-meet-carries-message-of-control-3331753 | Reuters characterized the 2024 NPC as signaling more control for Xi and a deeper focus on national security. This points to personalization and regime hardening, not liberalization. | 4B.10, 4B.8, 4B.5 |
| Strong negative | **Hong Kong “patriots-only” district council election** | South China Morning Post | 2024-04-17 | https://www.scmp.com/news/hong-kong/politics/article/3259258/first-hong-kong-district-council-poll-after-electoral-overhaul-cost-taxpayers-hk12-billion | The electoral overhaul produced a managed, low-turnout contest rather than a competitive local election. That is a clear sign of reduced democratic resilience. | 4B.10, 4B.1, 4B.4, 4B.7 |
| Strong negative | **Article 23 broadens Hong Kong security offenses** | Reuters | 2024-03-19 | https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/factboxscope-of-hong-kongs-new-national-security-laws-3344082 | Reuters said Article 23 widened sabotage, sedition, and state-secrets offenses and could impose life imprisonment. That expands the repression toolkit and weakens political freedom. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.3, 4B.9 |
| Strong negative | **RFA closes Hong Kong bureau after security-law concerns** | Reuters | 2024-03-29 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/usfunded-radio-free-asia-shuts-hong-kong-bureau-citing-security-law-concerns-3358157 | RFA closed its Hong Kong bureau over staff-safety concerns after Article 23; officials had called it a “foreign force.” That is direct chilling pressure on independent reporting. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.9 |
| Strong negative | **CAC self-media crackdown** | Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission Office | 2024-04-23 | https://www.cac.gov.cn/2024-04/23/c_1715545670217049.htm | The campaign ordered real-name verification, source labeling, AI labeling, traffic throttling, and account closures for “self-media.” That is a concrete digital-control escalation, not resilience-building. | 4B.10, 4B.6, 4B.9 |

**Bottom line**
- The pro-side record is procedural and rhetorical.
- The substantive 2024 record moves in the opposite direction: more Party control, less media autonomy, more coercive legal tools, and more managed politics in Hong Kong and on the mainland.
- On balance, Xi left political freedom and democratic resilience **weaker** than he inherited it.

**Search gap**
- I did not find credible 2024 evidence of reforms that genuinely broadened opposition space, strengthened independent oversight, or protected competitive politics.
- I also did not find evidence of a successful transition toward rule-bound succession; the available material points the other way.
